title: Analyzing Islamophobic Discourse Using Semi-Coded Terms and LLMs
benchmark_measurement: Detection and understanding of semi-coded Islamophobic hate speech, and a comparison of its toxicity score with antisemitic hate speech.
findings: Advanced LLMs like GPT-4 can understand semi-coded Islamophobic terms (e.g., muzrat, mudslime). Islamophobic posts were found to have higher toxicity scores on average than antisemitic posts based on Google's Perspective API. BERT topic modeling revealed that Islamophobic discourse is not purely religious but is intertwined with political, conspiratorial, and far-right movements, particularly targeting Muslim immigrants.
references: H. Mohideen and S. Mohideen, "The language of islamophobia in internet articles," Intellectual Discourse, vol. 16, no. 1, 2008.
